office_does: Klickitat PUD's three elected commissioners set policy, budgets and electric rates for the county-wide public utility, which also owns generation and transmission assets, for six-year terms.
race_blurb: Commissioner Dan Gunkel, on the board since 1991, runs on rate offsets from PUD-owned hydro and renewable natural gas and on finishing the Goldendale pumped-storage project. Logan Siebert, a Goldendale meat-processing business owner and first-time candidate, wants clearer explanations of rates and data centers that pay their share of grid costs. Siebert led the district primary 1,220 to 879; all of Klickitat County votes on the seat.

candidates.summary: Owner of Siebert Custom Slaughter and Meats in Goldendale and a reserve Goldendale police officer, running for office for the first time on rate transparency and protecting ratepayers.
highlights: Wants the PUD to explain how rates are set and why bills carry charges such as demand charges [S2]
Says data centers should 'pay their fair share for the grid' and not draw municipal or aquifer water [S2]
Questions how much PUD customers gain from private energy projects in the county [S2]
Led the district primary with 1,220 votes; the county Republican Party recommended him [S4][S5]
Owed $1,407.78 in 2025-2026 property taxes when the Sentinel asked in September [S3]

candidates.summary: Klickitat PUD commissioner since 1991, former Energy Northwest executive board member and owner of Gunkel Orchards, a third-generation family fruit farm.
highlights: Says PUD-owned assets now offset rates by about $5.9 million a year, about $34.49 a month for the average home [S2]
Says KPUD rates fell from third to tenth highest in its utility group during his tenure [S1]
Wants to see the Goldendale pumped-storage project completed [S1][S2]
Takes no campaign contributions and calls the party recommendation of his opponent 'inappropriate and sad' [S2]
Finished second in the district primary with 879 votes [S3]
